v5.1.74 Stable2026-11-16T18:34:09Z

A secret input or grant approval that settled while the relay link was down is now dismissed on the terminal that raised it after omo remote attach reconnects, instead of staying open with an answer the session would refuse. (#13773)

The computer-use conformance preflight test cleans up its compiled stand-in engine reliably on Windows. The test's temporary directory is now removed with the shared retrying helper, because Windows briefly keeps a just-run executable locked and Bun ignores rmSync's retry options. QA tooling only; no runtime behaviour changes. (#13299, part of #13221)

Fixed

  • The EQ.omo driver resolves a symlinked temp dir before it makes its sandboxes, so a recording on macOS no longer carries /private<sandbox> paths or an untrusted project. A new test fails when a platform's EQ.omo goldens were recorded with a senpi version more than a week away from the pinned one. (#13865)
  • CI: the desktop-bench comparison summary prints its regression thresholds (x1.3 and +0.5 ms) instead of undefined. It now reads them from compareBench's result rather than destructuring names eval-core.mjs does not export. (#13838, follow-up to #12876 review L1, #12567)
  • omo remote bootstrap installs device service 0.1.39 instead of 0.1.27, which was older than the wake and delivery minimum and answered open/create to the device with unsupported. (#13803)
  • A wake toward a device service older than the wake minimum now names the service's version, the minimum and the fix, instead of a bare unsupported. (#13803)
  • omo remote devices lists the device it runs on first (the account roster held only the other devices), and --json marks each row this_device. omo remote sessions --device with a device that is not on the account now fails with exit 2 naming it, instead of printing an empty list. (#13458, part of #13402)
  • thread_interrupt also stops the background jobs the interrupted turn started (a bash command it ran in the background or that auto-detached), so the thread no longer wakes a minute later when that job ends and replies as if it had never been interrupted. The result names what was stopped as background: { status: "stopped", stopped, failed }; an engine that predates the stop answers background: { status: "not_supported" }. A thread on this device and a thread on another device run the same interrupt code and answer the same shape. (#13444)
  • Computer use v3 (fake backend): the source guard that bans environment reads now also reports a grouped use std::{...} import of the environment module when a // or /* */ comment comes before the item inside the group. A comment can no longer hide an item, or split one at a comma or brace inside it. (#13363)
  • Desktop engine: the client retries a connection reset before the first reply byte only on Unix sockets, never on a Windows named pipe, where the daemon may already have run the request. (#12744)

Changed

  • The thread_read wait limit (600,000 ms) is now internal to the thread schema instead of an unused export; the limit itself is unchanged. No behavior change. (#13864)
  • Internal: the Windows backend documents when its posted key route still sends a key under a held Alt: for modifier-only chords, when releasing held keys, and while a failed Alt release is still recorded as held. A Windows test is also renamed to match the order of its checks. Nothing changes for users. (#13824, fixes #13821)
  • Internal: the module doc of the X11 input's client-process reader now names the /proc/<pid>/exe read added for the background-input check. Nothing changes for users. (#13820, fixes #13818)
  • /remote enable, /remote disable and /remote control in the TUI now answer in a sentence ("Remote sessions are on for this device.", "Remote control is off: ...") instead of the CLI's raw JSON. When /remote enable cannot finish, it shows the CLI's reason (for example "Could not download the OmO device service.") instead of an exit code, and a warning the CLI prints while succeeding (for example that the device is not linked) now shows after the result. (#13796)
  • The remote module's public types no longer depend on internal modules, so the importable remote SDK ships clean type declarations. No command or tool behaves differently. (#13782)
  • The remote module gains its client factories, one per kind of caller (a person, including omo remote; a session; a connector; the thread SDK's own principal; the device service's bootstrap entry), and its public entry. Its alias operations work when the caller hands in the account's alias registry, naming each session by the same durable id the thread tools use, and a device that does not answer is reported as offline rather than as having no such session. Nothing calls them yet, so no command or tool behaves differently. (#13750)
  • The remote module now declares every operation a surface needs (part 4a-2): opening, messaging, reading, following, waiting on, interrupting and closing a session on any device, its model and thinking level, attaching with pending approvals, aliases and the wake switch. The operations that have not landed yet answer "unsupported" as data, and nothing calls them yet, so no command or tool behaves differently. (#13747)
  • Remote access now has its own module (part 4a-1 of the one remote module design): typed results, one code list, a deadline table and a clock seam, with the service, devices and session list members. Nothing uses it yet, so no command or tool behaves differently. (#13498)
  • The device service client takes one injectable clock for its handshake, request, endpoint-command and attach waits, so each of those deadlines can be tested on fake time. Real timers stay the default and no wait changed. (#13473)
  • Computer use v3: on Windows, one user's two logon sessions take turns at the computer instead of acting at once: the interaction lock is now the operating system's file lock on %LOCALAPPDATA%\OmO\ComputerControl\run\interaction.lock, in a directory only that user and SYSTEM can open, on a local NTFS or ReFS volume. A session without a runtime directory cannot act on a real machine; it can still read. (#13367)
  • The Windows live tier's ledger job now fails when a fresh measurement's verdict differs from the committed crates/omo-computer-backend-win32/probes/hosted-windows-live.tsv, naming each leg that moved, so the committed ledger only changes on purpose. (#13274, part of #13221)

Added

  • Computer use v3: the session crate's side-effect funnel lands. Every mutating call runs the gate, writes a pre-input marker before the first OS call on every transport, performs the call, reads back and writes one audit event per side effect; a crashed call is never resent and reads delivery_uncertain. Audit, lock, permits, batches and artifact retention come with it, and a typed secret is audited by length only. Nothing user-visible changes yet; the existing desktop engine is untouched. (#13367)
  • Computer use v3: the safety crate omo-computer-safety lands. It holds the fixed gate order (each gate refuses before any OS call with nothing sent), the supervisor whose stop commit releases every hold within 1 s or exits, the stop latch and persisted stop marker under the per-uid state root, the live/deaf/none stop paths with the host-relay-only policy, the per-OS protected tables and dangerous chords, and the self set. The walking skeleton's click and typeText now pass through the gate. Nothing user-visible changes yet; the existing desktop engine is untouched. (#13353)
  • Computer use v3: the walking skeleton lands. omo-computer-engine runs on the fake backend with --stdio (NDJSON JSON-RPC), --schema, --selftest and --version; the session answers session.open, capabilities and close plus the thin click and typeText verbs; refusals go through the closed COMPUTER_* table. script/qa/computer/replay.ts replays conformance cases against the engine binary and prints the JSON pointer of the first mismatch. Nothing user-visible changes yet; the existing desktop engine is untouched. (#13352)
  • Spike SP-R probe and ledger for the computer-use relay pipe: auth lifetime, hub hibernation, message-size and liveness limits measured against a local relay, plus read-only checks on a same-network pair and the hosted relay. Probe-only, no engine change. (#13166, part of #13051)
  • Computer use v3: spike SP-W adds a Wayland probe and its ledger under crates/omo-computer-backend-wayland/probes/. The probe measures, in one container per compositor (GNOME 46, KDE Plasma 6, sway), whether portal restore tokens survive restarts, which portals exist, libei regions, a second ConnectToEIS, the clipboard grant, key release when an input owner dies, the GNOME extension and accessibility behaviour, and KWin window-management access. Each fact is one cited ledger row. Nothing user-visible changes. (#13163)
  • Desktop engine: several clients run by the same user can attach to one shared --serve daemon session (SDK attach over the Unix socket), each with its own replies; the daemon checks every client's peer credentials and closes a connection from another user before any byte. (#12744)

Release provenance

  • v5.1.74 is published from abf50be3e7ec62019c4315acb0f087413983d583: the CI-receipted release-state head 243acc0da00a05d9480f35045cb2678ca0001925 plus #13928's operator-built darwin workflow change, which touches .github/workflows only (6 files, 0 outside). The package bytes are identical to the receipted head, and the darwin artifacts are operator-built from 243acc0da00a05d9480f35045cb2678ca0001925.
  • These workflows predate #13915: the release tag is created inside the publish-main job rather than in a separate job before any platform package is published. The dispatch was checked to have no existing tag pointing at a different sha.

v5.1.73 Stable2026-11-16T17:17:49Z

Remote session views stop receiving each streamed delta twice. open_session for a remote create, open, or fork now goes on the endpoint dialer (a fresh connection per call, closed once it settles), instead of sharing the long-lived connection the later session.attach rides on; opening on the shared connection had attached the host's delegated engine connection to the session as well, so the engine wrote every delta twice. A connection a caller lends is now named borrowed, so the CLI's one shared connection survives the open. (#13761, adopting #13075 by @surlymochan)

The first session on a newly enabled device now starts memory sync. Sync used to start before the memory repository existed, fail to write its space binding, log "memory sync failed to start" and never retry; it now waits for the repository and starts on its own once the first memory write creates it. (#13493, fixes #13486) (#13627)

Memory sync drops a replaced desktop account cleanly. When the desktop moved to another account without announcing a retirement, the engine opened the new account but left the old one half alive: it kept listening on the desktop channel and its open sync sessions did not end. The old account now ends as soon as the engine sees it is no longer current, which also ends its sessions. In a session Worker, an operation started just before the desktop retired its account can no longer hand back a handle from the old account. (#13334, follow-up to #13327 and #13329) (#13627)

OmO is ready to load on the tool side of a split session: its first-paint startup gate is declared for the agent-loop side, so the tool side never registers those handlers, and on the tool side deferred startup work runs right away instead of waiting for a paint that never comes; local sessions register exactly as before. (#12329) (#13627)

Computer use is ready for the tool side of a split session: foreground control is revoked, and the engine session ended, when the run of the session holding it ends or that session closes, through that session's own lifecycle instead of loop events; local sessions behave exactly as before. (#12328) (#13627)

Adds the executable proof that computer use returns one screenshot per tool call, under today's capture caps and unchanged across the tool side of a split session; no behavior change. (#12337) (#13627)

Computer use is ready for the tool side of a split session: there, foreground control follows the device's own exec setting (refused until exec is enabled on that device, then granted to any session without a per-session confirm); local sessions keep today's confirm exactly. (#12332) (#13627)

Computer use is ready for the tool side of a split session: sessions sharing one device take its foreground one at a time, and only the holder can release it; local sessions behave exactly as before. (#12339) (#13627)

Computer use is ready for the tool side of a split session: a missing OS permission (Screen Recording, Accessibility) raised there is reported to the session that owns the call, once per permission, without a session marker on that side; local sessions behave exactly as before. (#12450) (#13627)

Computer use v3: the result contract refuses a receipt under an unverified delivery and types refusal reasons. An ActionReport that carries a consumption receipt under not_delivered, delivered_unverified or unknown/unknown (#13147) is now refused, both when it is built and when it is parsed from the wire. A backend refusal's reason is the closed Reason type, so a mistyped reason is a compile error. (#13137)

  • CI: a computer-use bench regression job compares the desktop bench against a base and fails on a p50 regression above 30%; it runs nightly against the newest release tag and on manual dispatch, not on pull requests. (#12876)

A question or approval a remote session asks now reaches every omo remote attach on it, not only the one that sent the prompt. The terminal UI shows the request and sends your answer back by its request id, as it already did for prompts you sent yourself, and dismisses it when another device answers it first. A secret input or a grant approval is still shown only on the terminal whose prompt raised it. A request already waiting when you attach, or raised while the relay link was down, is shown too, and one that was settled during a relay gap is dismissed after the reconnect (#13474). (#12750)

Changed

  • The ulw-plan plan template and reference, ulw-execute's decomposition step, and the Codex edition's ulw-loop reference and plan agent no longer say "target 5-8 per wave; fewer than 3 means under-splitting". A wave is sized to the tasks that are independent of each other. (#13851)
  • The mass-ulw skill's listing description now says a graph is sized to the request with one run per phase, matching the rewritten skill body; it no longer says each phase's stages are defined up front in one run. (#13848)
  • ulw-loop no longer tells HEAVY goals to target 5-8 tasks per wave or treats fewer than 3 as under-splitting; a wave is sized to the tasks that are independent of each other. Mass research gives lead nodes the same handoff file and source tagging as harvest nodes, and both ulw-research editions make slice reducers conditional like the mass-ulw planning reference does. (#13847)
  • mass-ulw now sizes the workflow graph to the request: a small graph by default, a verification node only when the final check is too long to run inline, per-item chains instead of a review node between waves, and mass research that starts from the angles the topic has instead of a 60-angle floor. The skill and its planning reference were rewritten and are about a quarter shorter. (#13834)
  • Internal: the desktop service's fake engine and test harness are now the ./testing package export of senpi-desktop-service, and the computer-use tests in omo-senpi and senpi-desktop-tool import them from there instead of a relative path into its test tree. Nothing changes for users. (fixes #13614) (#13712)
  • Memory sync: a test now covers a remote head that arrives on the stream while a sync cycle is running and is not applied by it, so the engine must run exactly one more cycle to pick it up; a lost wakeup there now fails the test. No behavior change. (#13656, fixes #11778)
  • Remote sessions are now on by default. The moment omo login completes it switches them on for this device and says so in one line ("Remote is on for this device: other signed-in devices can reach it. Turn off: omo remote disable"), and every omo start keeps the device set up. omo remote disable turns them off and remembers that, so neither a later omo login nor an omo start turns them on again; omo remote enable turns them back on (#13594). (#13602) (#13627)
  • device-service-core's local-API tests fail when omo starts sending a request type that has no reply row in the LA21 decoding test or that the conformance test owner still lists as unserved (#13491). (#13491)
  • omo remote, the thread tools and the memory sync use the device service's own local-API client, vendored byte for byte from omo-relay-daemon (main after #1115, plus the read-side tolerance of omo-relay-daemon#1130), instead of a hand-edited copy; a guard test keeps that client and the connection factories behind the device-service layer (#13475). (#13475)

Fixed

  • A fanout that fails as a whole (an unknown or ambiguous target, invalid options, a duplicate target under dedup: "reject") and a target that runs past timeoutMs get the same typed error, and a failed resultOf names the request instead of treating its op id as a device. (#13813)
  • The shipped device account, device service, memory sync, wake, thread client and bunshin bundles, and the omo-ai launcher's sign-in module (omo login / logout / whoami), are rebuilt from their current sources, so the released plugin and launcher no longer lag the code merged into dev. (#13810)
  • The shipped thread client and thread SDK bundles now carry the session-only model change from #13494, so switching a remote session's model no longer rewrites the target device's default model in the released build. (#13786)
  • Memory: a contender recovering a lock from a dead owner no longer fails when that lock file is already gone by the time it removes it (seen on Windows, where memory reflection supervisors then failed admission). Any other removal error still surfaces. (#13745, fixes #11644)
  • Device operations run through the bundled fleet SDK (bunshin in eval cells) now fail with a typed error, { code, message, next_action } like the thread tools, instead of an internal transport sentence. The message names the operation and the device, and the code tells a wrong argument (invalid_arguments) apart from an offline device (device_offline), a policy refusal (scope_denied) and a lost connection (transport_closed). The relay's own op-result codes pass through unchanged and carry uncertain when the device may have run the op. The "no transport" error and a failed connect now say what to do next. (#13744)
  • Computer use on X11 no longer reports a background click, scroll, drag, typing or key chord as delivered when the target app drops synthetic input (GTK 3/4, Qt, LibreOffice, Chromium, Electron and Firefox apps whose window class names no toolkit, and xterm, whose allowSendEvents setting no other app can read). Background input now goes only to apps whose toolkit is known to accept it (Xt and Motif apps other than xterm, Tk); any other app is refused before anything is sent, with the element action and foreground delivery offered as the next step. (#13736, addresses #9109)
  • On Windows, background keyboard input that holds Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win while another key goes down is now refused with BackgroundUnavailable and nothing sent, instead of being reported delivered while the application received only the bare key. This covers key chords such as ctrl+k, bounded key and mouse holds with such keys, and a single character the keyboard layout types with Shift or AltGr (for example K, or @ on a German layout). Send it with delivery: "foreground" or use accessibility actions. (#13734, fixes #13297)
  • On Linux, the computer tool's desktop.elementAt(x, y) now returns the element under the point, such as a GTK window's Press button, instead of the window's untitled root filler at every point. (#13732, fixes #13296)
  • With real hit-test answers, the check that an element is not covered before an accessibility action now works on Linux too: another element of the same window across the target's centre refuses the action with occluded, as on macOS. The target's own descendants, such as a list row wider than the list's viewport, never count as covering it, on any platform where the backend can compare elements. (#13732)
  • Memory that two devices already held as the same text, such as the default files every memory starts with, no longer appears twice after the devices start syncing one space. A device joining a space now merges its own copy of a file into the shared one line by line, keeping every line of both and the lines they share once. (#13730, fixes #13725)
  • A launch spec that lists no extensions now gives its host the same runtime build id as omo host ensure predicts. The compiled binary still added its own plugin folder to that host's command line, so the two ids disagreed for such a spec. (#13729)
  • Memory in a folder with no git remote, and memory from a session outside any project, now syncs between your signed-in devices through one account default space instead of staying on the device that wrote it. A repository that had its own per-device space moves to the account space once and sends its memory there. (#13726, fixes #13720)
  • A host the compiled omo binary starts now reports the same runtime build id as the omo host ensure that started it. The binary added its own plugin folder to the host's command line on top of the launch spec, so with no spec, or with a copy of the spec, the host and the CLI disagreed: the desktop app judged its own engine a build mismatch and every handover's replacement host exited. (#13700)
  • The omo-native trust test suites no longer fail when the test runner's TMPDIR is group-writable: each suite now runs with a private temporary directory the trust stage accepts (#13697). (#13698)
  • omo remote open --model now sets the model on the session it just created even when its durable ID differs from its relay listing key. Send, model, interrupt, close and attach accept both the durable ID returned by open --json and <device>/<session>; the durable ID is the documented canonical identity. (#13666)
  • omo remote now prints the credential store's own message when it cannot read your sign-in, such as the omo account forget hint for an invalid stored sign-in or the note that the OS credential store is locked or unreachable, instead of only the generic notice. (#13644, fixes #13638)
  • omo remote wake --help now gives the switch's real default: waking is on unless you turn it off. It said "off unless turned on", which never matched the device service. (#13637)
  • A session host start no longer times out when its supervisor or host child has to re-run the engine trust step: the re-run keeps the startup pipe the launcher reads, instead of losing it and reporting supervisor_bootstrap / host_bootstrap timeouts for a healthy host (#13622). (#13632)
  • Thread gateway: the omo daemon registers this device's agent dir at start-up even when senpi reports its endpoint registry as a relative or unnormalized path. It falls back to the launcher's agent dir with one warning instead of registering nothing (#13604). (#13609) (#13627)
  • Memory keeps working after an extension hot reload, for example when a watched SKILL.md changes (#13098). The reloaded extension no longer fails to register memory with session worker data "omo.memory-sync.v1" is already provided. (#13101) (#13627)
  • omob dev builds bundle one senpi engine again: the build linked the source-built engine only at the root while omo-native, omo-senpi, senpi-task and omo-opencode kept the registry copy, so the trust hand-off was lost and every coordinated session host start timed out in supervisor_bootstrap (#13620). (#13621)
  • thread_set_model, omo remote model and omo remote open --model changed the target device's default model along with the session's. The engine record now carries scope: "session", so only the addressed session switches models. thread_set_reasoning likewise no longer rewrites the level the device remembers for the model; it changes only that session's level. (#13494)
  • A waiting omo remote send no longer reports its turn as interrupted because an earlier run in the same session was interrupted. (#13481)
  • A waiting omo remote send no longer prints the turn's answer twice when the answer is both streamed and already stored in the transcript: the transcript read is not printed once the stream printed this turn's text. (#13481)
  • A waiting omo remote send no longer prints an earlier identical message's answer as its own when that earlier run finished just before the send was answered: only a finish that follows this send's own prompt ends its wait. (#13481)
  • A waiting omo remote send no longer prints an earlier identical message's answer when that earlier message carried no client message id (a send without --wait, text typed in the TUI), and a send whose interrupted turn was followed by a later message still prints its partial answer after the later turn's text. (#13481)
  • A waiting omo remote send to an engine that stores no client message id prints a turn that finished before the send was answered and exits, instead of waiting until the session closes; an interrupted turn whose partial answer only partly streamed prints the rest of it. (#13481)
  • A first waiting omo remote send into a session whose earlier identical message was typed in the TUI or sent without --wait no longer prints that earlier message's answer when the engine stores no client message id: a message already in the session before the send is never taken as the send's own (an identical message stored between the send starting and its prompt landing is still indistinguishable, oh-my-openagent#13580). (#13481)
  • While OmO accounts are closed, omo logout --help and omo whoami --help print their own help and exit 0, as omo login --help does, instead of the login refusal; any other argument is still refused. (#13466, fixes #13461) (#13466)
  • In the standalone omo binary, the kill guard's check (omo __kill-guard check ..., run by the guard before a kill, pkill or killall) now reaches the engine's judge instead of being read as a chat prompt, so the guard allows or refuses the signal as it does in the npm install. (#13460, fixes #13449) (#13460)
  • thread_list and omo thread list now list threads on all of the account's devices in every call, not only with all_scope. An ended thread on another device shows as resumable instead of live. The result includes the account's devices: name, platform, kind, online state, last seen, thread count, and whether this listing reached them, so a device that did not answer is named instead of silently missing. omo thread list --json now prints that whole result as one object (threads, devices, remote_unavailable) instead of a bare array of threads, and the plain listing names each other device's thread's device and prints one line per device. (#13394, fixes #13392)
  • Computer use v3 (fake backend): inject() now refuses a scripted failure whose code and reason have no row in the error table, the same check the scenario loader applies, instead of failing later. A capture whose extent is under one whole pixel (an empty size or region, or any length that scales to less than 1 px), or whose scale is zero or negative, or whose size or region is negative, now refuses CaptureFailed before allocating instead of returning a 0x0 frame or, for a negative size times a negative scale, a positive one. The fake's source guard now also bans environment reads, including a grouped use std::{...} import of the module (on one line or split across lines) and any path into it. (#13133) (#13120)
  • cu-eval live runs now restore and tear down every task on every exit path, close the apps before deleting their scratch files, and list any restore step that failed in the row's restoreErrors. (#12849)

Added

  • The relay transport re-vendored in #13744 also brought in new public surface: createRelayTransport takes retryUnreachableMs (how long a device whose describe failed is listed unsupported before it is asked again, default 30 s), and the transport it returns has uploadArtifact(bytes) and fetchArtifact, which carry pushTree / pullTree archives over the relay. (#13813)

  • A new thread can be started with its model, thinking level, approval mode and first message in one step, on this device or on another of your devices: thread_create takes model, reasoning, permission_preset, prompt and delivery, and omo remote open takes --model, --thinking, --worktree (with --branch and --base) and --prompt. A model the device cannot run now refuses the create and leaves no session behind, instead of opening one on the default model; an agent can keep or narrow its own approval mode for the thread it creates, never widen it. (#13748)

  • The session id omo remote open prints now works with every other omo remote verb right away. send, model, interrupt, close and attach accept the durable thread_id on its own (its device is found in the account listing) or as <device>/<session>, and a session opened a moment ago is no longer answered "no session". A thread created with a first message gets that message even before its device lists the new session. (#13748)

  • An agent can be woken by a session on another device of your account: monitor({ type: "rpc", target: "<device>/<session>" }) reports its status changes and turn ends as they happen, and after a relay drop, a device-service restart or an engine restart it reports what changed meanwhile, once. <session> can be the thread id thread_list shows, an alias, or the session's key; <device>/* follows every session on that device. (#13743, #12719)

  • thread_read takes wait_ms: for a thread on another device it first waits, up to that bound, until it sees the thread's turn end (not a momentary idle), then returns the transcript with how the wait ended (settled with the turn_id it saw end, timeout, cancelled or ended). (#13743, #13417)

  • /remote inside the TUI: list this account's devices and sessions, open a session on another device, send it a message and see the reply, interrupt or close it, change its model, and turn remote on or off, without leaving OmO. A bare /remote walks you from a device to a session to what to do with it. /remote attach names the command to run in a new terminal. (#13741)

  • Memory sync can now parse, derive and redact recovery-phrase keys: a 24-word BIP39 English encoding of 32 random bytes, keys derived with HKDF-SHA-256 bound to the account, and fixed test vectors. Nothing creates a phrase key yet; turning on sync with a recovery phrase lands in a later change. (#13330) (#13627)

  • Memory sync can create a recovery-phrase first device: turning sync on takes a method (passkey or recovery phrase), shows a void notice that survives crashes when a shown phrase was not saved, and sends a sync capability header. Creating a phrase stays off behind a client flag and a service floor check until the service side is ready. (#13335) (#13627)

  • Memory sync can recover with a recovery phrase and enroll, rotate or remove phrase keys from a member device; creating a phrase stays behind the client flag and service floor check. (#13336) (#13627)

  • macOS live QA: a Chrome two-window typing scenario checks that background typing lands in the second window and leaves the first one untouched and key. (#12823) (#13627)

  • macOS live QA: a dense-window observe scenario checks that a page with 5,000+ accessibility nodes returns a partial snapshot at the deadline, drills into a cut, and keeps the default skeleton within its token budget. (#12823) (#13627)

  • The live macOS QA driver's --list flag prints every scenario name on any host. (#12823) (#13627)

  • The live macOS QA driver's --dense-rows <n> flag sets how many rows the dense-window page renders (default 2,000). (#12823) (#13627)

  • Desktop engine: a request size cap, a frame cap and an idle flush keep long sessions bounded (P12b). (#12807) (#13627)

  • Computer use v3: spike SP-B ships a probe ledger that classifies the ten bunshin hosting gaps as closed, open with a plan row, or needing an installer change, and records which host owes each condition it cannot measure. No engine code changes and nothing user-visible changes. (#13156)

  • Computer use v3: the SP-T spike probe for macOS lands under crates/omo-computer-backend-macos/probes/. It is a Bun probe with shell helpers and a ledger, and it asks which process TCC charges for the computer-use launcher, which client_type the grant records, whether a grant survives a generation swap and a rebuild, and which launchd session the launcher lands in. Every ledger row is still unmeasured, waiting for a macOS 26 host with a QA account and a person at its session. No engine code and nothing user-visible changes. (#13143)

  • Computer use v3: the scriptable fake backend lands in omo-computer-backend-fake. It provides one scenario format with typed, JSON-pointer refusals for an unknown key, a non-object root, a dangling window and an error-code pair the table does not have; a recording sink that writes every OS-level side effect as one line; a fake clock driven only by OMO_COMPUTER_FAKE_CLOCK; timelines for loading indicators, observer events and user input; a fault FIFO whose refusals resolve through the COMPUTER_* table; and macos, x11, wayland and win32 personas. Every scenario field has a fixture and a null control. Nothing user-visible changes yet; the existing desktop engine is untouched. (#13120)

  • A latency bench and the 7-task cu-eval for computer-use v2 (P13b). (#12849)

opendatalab/MinerU ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
mineru-4.2.3-releasedMinerU 4.2.3 Stable2026-11-16T18:13:18Z

4.2.3

  • 新增单文件执行超时与托管恢复。WebUI、Router 和 API Server 支持 --task-timeout，默认 3600 秒，从取得解析名额开始计时，覆盖解析和服务端产物打包。超时任务返回 task_timeout，独立 API 停止接收新任务，由部署方重建服务。Router 通过父进程监督回收超时 worker 及模型子进程，并重新启动服务，即使执行线程、事件循环或取消清理挂起也能触发恢复。
  • 改善 WebUI 恢复体验与进程清理。本地 WebUI 由 Router 托管唯一 worker，恢复期间显示状态，尚未提交的排队请求在服务就绪后继续。旧 worker 上其他未完成请求返回 worker_restarted，问题文件可手动重试。完善 Windows 进程树、临时目录与控制通道回收，明确报告模型预加载失败，并在连续三次启动恢复失败后停止自动重试。
  • 修复 Doclib 全文检索被图片载荷挤占。构造检索文本时提取正文、公式和图表说明，再应用字符预算，避免内嵌图片的 base64 内容占满索引而遗漏正文。升级后从解析缓存重建已有索引，并保留跨页内容续接。缓存不完整的文档会记录迁移原因，补齐缓存或重新解析后重启 Doclib 可继续迁移。
  • 提前检查 vLLM 与 Transformers 兼容性。启动引擎前识别 vllm<0.29.0 与 transformers>=5.23.0 的不兼容组合，并给出升级 vLLM 或调整 Transformers 版本范围的明确提示，减少模型加载阶段难以定位的失败。
  • 更新 DocVortex 依赖。最低版本提升至 0.6.24，同步原生文档解析与共享渲染能力的改进。

配置提示。Router 的 --worker-tier 默认改为 auto，由各 worker 根据自己的设备环境确定档位上限。需要固定上限时可显式指定 flash、basic、standard 或 advanced。--task-timeout 必须为正整数，上传、排队、客户端下载及模型启动预加载各自使用独立的等待与生命周期设置。

4.2.3

  • Add per-file execution timeouts and managed recovery. WebUI, Router, and API Server support --task-timeout, defaulting to 3600 seconds from acquiring an execution slot through parsing and server-side artifact packaging. Timed-out tasks return task_timeout. A standalone API stops accepting new work and relies on its deployment host to recreate the service. Router supervises local workers from the parent process, reclaims timed-out workers and model subprocesses, and restarts the service even when execution threads, the event loop, or cancellation cleanup stall.
  • Improve WebUI recovery and process cleanup. Local WebUI uses Router to manage a single worker, displays recovery status, and resumes queued requests awaiting submission once the service is ready. Other unfinished requests on the replaced worker return worker_restarted, and affected files can be retried manually. Improve Windows process-tree, temporary-directory, and control-channel cleanup, surface model preload failures, and stop automatic recovery after three consecutive startup failures.
  • Keep image payloads out of Doclib full-text indexes. Build search text from body content, formulas, and figure or table descriptions before applying the character budget, preventing embedded image base64 data from crowding out searchable text. Rebuild existing indexes from cached parse results during upgrade while preserving cross-page continuations. Documents with incomplete caches record a migration reason and can resume migration after restoring or reparsing the cache and restarting Doclib.
  • Check vLLM and Transformers compatibility before startup. Detect the incompatible combination of vllm<0.29.0 and transformers>=5.23.0 before engine initialization, with actionable guidance to upgrade vLLM or select a compatible Transformers range.
  • Update DocVortex. Raise the minimum version to 0.6.24 for native document parsing and shared rendering improvements.

Configuration note. Router now defaults --worker-tier to auto, allowing each worker to select its tier ceiling from its device environment. Specify flash, basic, standard, or advanced for a fixed ceiling. --task-timeout requires a positive integer. Uploads, queueing, client downloads, and model startup preloading use their own waiting and lifecycle settings.

升级 / Upgrade

pip install -U "mineru==4.2.3"

debpalash/VoiceStudio ↗ 1 release · 1 prerelease
v0.5.9-beta.5v0.5.9-beta.5 — VoiceStudio Prerelease2026-11-16T15:26:22Z

Download

Platform Download Signing
Windows x64 Installer ⚠️ Unsigned: SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC"; choose More info → Run anyway
Windows ARM64 (experimental) Installer ⚠️ Unsigned: SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC"; choose More info → Run anyway
macOS Apple Silicon DMG ✅ Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple
macOS Intel DMG ✅ Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple
Linux x64 AppImage · deb — Linux packages are not code-signed
Android APK · AAB ✅ Signed APK (signature verified); AAB is the Play upload bundle
iPhone Unsigned IPA ⚠️ Unsigned: sign it with your own Apple ID to sideload; not a TestFlight build

This beta adds separately opted-in automatic error reports, so failures can reach the maintainers without a manual bug report. Reports stay off unless you allow them, and never include audio, text, files, names, credentials or logs.

Highlights

  • Optional automatic error reports stay off until separately allowed in Privacy
  • Android Stories and Audiobook keep long manuscripts scrollable and recover drafts through activity recreation
  • Stories can merge adjacent lines with compatible speaker and voice settings
  • Linux ROCm setup preserves its installed PyTorch stack, and GPU readiness reflects failed self-tests
  • Phone dub exports check available space and avoid false low-space errors on iOS

Upgrading: install over the existing app or use Settings → Updates → Beta. Voices, projects, settings and installed models stay in place.

Changed

  • Removed an unused legacy update-busy helper while retaining active restart protection (#4149) — thanks @themrbeasley!
  • Retired an unused legacy update toast while preserving the active Electron update controls (#4141) — thanks @themrbeasley!
  • Retired the unreachable legacy shared UI and the guard tests that held it, repointing the live-behaviour guards to the renderer, and dropped 12 unused npm packages (#4095)
  • Smaller install: removed unused leftover images and old helper code from the app source (#4087)
  • Projects grid view stays smooth with thousands of items by drawing only the cards in view (#4079)
  • Long Projects, dub project and Transcribe history lists now render only the rows on screen, so they stay fast with thousands of items (#4074)
  • Idle CPU: a hidden or minimised window no longer runs polling timers or elapsed-time clocks, and they refresh once when it is shown again (#4073)
  • Removed unused renderer files and 477 unused translation strings, and locale:check now fails on an English key no code uses (#4047)
  • Removed more unused legacy shared components, utilities and API helpers from the old shared UI folder (#4045)
  • Local-model folder saves no longer unload the engine when the stored folder did not change (#4043)
  • Removed more unused legacy settings, gallery and engine screens from the old shared UI folder (#4042)
  • Idle polling is relaxed: the backend health probe slows when steady, cloud-sync polling pauses while the window is hidden, and the Windows parent watcher polls less often (#4041)
  • Removed more unused legacy dubbing screens and hooks from the old shared UI folder (#4040)
  • Release notes now open with one Download table listing every desktop and phone download with its signing, followed by the Highlights (#4037)
  • Removed about 25,000 lines of unused legacy interface code, two unused font packages and the always-skipped weekly evals job; the app itself is unchanged (#2603, #4032)

Added

  • Stories can merge adjacent lines with the same speaker and compatible voice/speed settings while preserving text and inline directions — thanks cvak on Discord! (#4161)
  • Added separately opted-in failure reporting through Supermetry app intake across desktop, mobile and server installs, with private metadata and consent-controlled retries (#4137)
  • Dubbing exports the selected transcript as plain UTF-8 TXT, including edited text before generating a dub, with native Save As and paired phone sharing. (#4155) — thanks @shivamdhiman999111-source!
  • A dub interrupted by a crash or restart now picks up from its finished segments instead of starting over (#4088)
  • omnivoice-gguf now supports voice design, non-verbal tags and the decode-steps slider (#4084) — thanks @snazzybean!
  • Cebuano is now a dub translation target (#4058, #4072) — thanks @onparr-24!
  • Home shows a What's new link, winter pixel snow, a Christmas-week Santa, two rows of contributor portraits, and an easter egg that hides the credits until the next update after you visit three contributor profiles (#4070)
  • Voice Cloning has a generation queue: takes started while one is rendering wait their turn and run one after another — thanks @ItzSudhan! (#4064)
  • Audiobooks and Stories have a New project button that starts an empty draft without touching saved projects (#4055)

Docs

  • The localization contract no longer exempts the removed legacy shared i18n catalog, which pointed reviewers at a path that does not exist (#4186) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • Document the enforced up-to-date merge gate while the repository cannot use GitHub merge queues (#4165)
  • Track the unresolved VoxCPM2 installation report separately from GPU fallback fixes, reported by vinhson (#4154)
  • Track the unresolved Windows model-loading crash and distinguish merged installer repairs from released fixes (#4146) — thanks @renaldyramadani123-code!
  • Installation tracking separates shipped fixes, pending repairs and unresolved report evidence (#4121)
  • Document host-managed Tailscale access for Docker without sharing the host daemon socket (#4111) — thanks @MaverickKB!

Fixed

  • Desktop failure observers retain the original consent during backend restarts and preserve normal Promise behavior. (#4209)
  • CosyVoice catalogue downloads skip unused alternative model files and use the same required assets as managed installs. (#4207)
  • Android keeps large manuscripts editable and recoverable, and retains reporting consent through permission prompts. (#4206) — thanks @gaino-svg!
  • The closed-PR CI sweep requests cancellations incrementally, preserves partial progress and reports incomplete searches or skipped requests accurately (#4189) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • Kept automatic error reports bound to original consent through delayed work and recovery, and preserved native CI verification (#4184) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • Windows ROCm setup preserves working-install stamps, verifies the pinned interpreter, and reports native crash exit codes (#4182) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • Windows checkouts no longer fail the CLI packaging tests: the Debian maintainer-script cases skip when the host has no POSIX shell or symlink privileges (#4178) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • Phone dubbing clip/stem exports check output space on both platforms and avoid false low-space errors on iOS (#4168)
  • Linux ROCm setup skips CUDA downloads and preserves its installed PyTorch stack on resume (#4167) — thanks @khryztiam!
  • GPU readiness and in-process routing reflect completed self-test failures (#4166) — thanks @khryztiam!
  • CLA audits keep exempt accounts visible for provenance review without reporting a missing required signature (#4164)
  • Release rehearsals show measured Android APK signing, and tagged downloads require matching signature evidence (#4163)
  • Manual Windows crash reports retain the faulting thread ahead of verbose status tails — thanks @renaldyramadani123-code and @freemood36-svg! (#4162)
  • macOS publishing checks Gatekeeper even when Windows installers are explicitly unsigned (#4153)
  • The reviewed model-install steps now require the same authenticated consumer as the rest of the model manager (#4152) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • Diagnostic bundles and Electron bug reports redact share PINs and encoded credential query parameters (#4151) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • Make the installed-model licence action open its terms and acknowledgement dialog — thanks hugotriunfa18 on Discord! (#4147)
  • Android model downloads resume through VPNs while preserving Wi-Fi policy and saved ranges (#4140) — thanks @JerryTimi!
  • Stopped playback errors from incorrectly claiming that generated audio files are missing (#4138) — thanks @AAYUSH-CODER1904!
  • Transcriptions can save clean plain text and timed SRT captions, with an explanation when subtitle timings are unavailable (#4135)
  • Cloud sign-in now rejects a discovery document whose token or revocation endpoint is not on the issuer's own origin (#4133) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • Segmented model downloads pin public destinations with bounded DNS checks across redirects, ranges and proxies, preventing private-network fallback and CDN credential leaks (#4132) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • The LM Studio model probe no longer sends the stored API key in clear text to a remote host unless plaintext LAN is allowed (#4131) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • A deterministic test now fails when a new mutating API route ships without an authorization decision (#4130) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • Docker deployments now require the administrator API key for the runtime log, log stream, recent errors and crash report, as the install docs already said (#4129) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • MCP tools preserve remote caller permissions across local and HTTP backends, including failed transport lookups (#4128) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • TTS and event WebSockets now enforce the same loopback/credential rule as dictation, closing a share-PIN bypass (#4126) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • Imported project bundles can no longer make ffmpeg fetch remote URLs through a playlist-shaped media file (#4125) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • Deleting history, rewriting dub scripts and clearing model-licence receipts now require an administrator, as the API docs already promised (#4124) — thanks @DeryFerd!

  • Model deletion over the API now requires administrator rights (#4122) — thanks @DeryFerd!
  • Crash recurrence reports recognize current Electron version fields and distinguish beta releases (#4120)
  • Reclaim idle GPU models before generation when VRAM or RAM is low (#4117) — thanks @vandyahmad24!
  • Model downloads reject damaged files and retry without reusing corrupt ranges, while cancellation preserves verified work (#4116)
  • Reuse verified setup wheels on low-space retries and handle interrupted size probes without an uncaught error. (#4115)
  • Saved and inline pronunciation choices apply consistently across speech, dubbing, batch and voice-conversion routes (#4114) — thanks @nntloc!
  • Stop cancelled setup retries promptly and keep verbose runtime probes from blocking on their diagnostic output. (#4113)
  • Long recordings use duration-scaled transcription limits across uploads, dubbing, child engines and MCP tools (#4112) — thanks @xabiherdz-svg!
  • URL imports restore their connection guard after temporary DNS resolver changes (#4110)
  • Update the optional Dagger pipeline's OpenTelemetry dependencies to fix excessive CPU use when parsing malformed trace context. (#4109)
  • Optional analytics no longer delays backend readiness, and consent changes invalidate queued startup work (#4108) — thanks @cf3901646!
  • Auto setup can retry PyPI failures through the regional mirror and report the actual failed host (#4107) — thanks @mrkeshi!
  • Malformed model-install status responses keep the interface open and preserve the last valid download state (#4106) — thanks @ftlcustomerservice73-ui!
  • Windows installer process checks skip custom PowerShell profiles, and source installs use shorter build paths to avoid MSVC linker failures (#4099)
  • Restarting to install an update keeps update status available while the local engine shuts down, avoiding missing-handler errors (#4098)
  • Automatic blank-renderer recovery keeps the open workspace instead of returning Stories or Audiobook to Home (#4097)
  • Dubbing keeps the saved recording for cloned and designed voices with style instructions, so each segment uses the selected speaker's reference (#4093)
  • Setup on Auto-detect now retries a stalled Python download (cpython-… (download)) once from the other source, GitHub or its mirror, instead of stalling again (#4085)
  • A refused cross-site API request now names its origin and gives the exact OMNIVOICE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS line to add, so other local apps such as AIRI can be connected (#4083)
  • Setup no longer crashes with "Cannot set property code" when a runtime download or check is cancelled on Windows (#4082)

  • When the operating system times out starting the engine (spawn ETIMEDOUT, seen on macOS), VoiceStudio retries twice and then says to restart the computer (#4039)
  • Settings → Updates lists only your channel's releases, and Beta suggests switching to Stable when a newer stable is out (#4038)
